4916204e-065f-4c4c-aca6-5118f5caa517.name: Azzinoth
4916204e-065f-4c4c-aca6-5118f5caa517.brief_description: A dark, foreboding temple devoted to the Scurge Lord Radan, shrouded in perpetual gloom.
4916204e-065f-4c4c-aca6-5118f5caa517.description:
Azzinoth rises from a bleak, windswept plateau, its walls hewn from black basalt that seems to drink the light. A perpetual gloom hangs over the temple, the sky forever overcast with low, rolling clouds that let through only a thin, sickly gray light. The outer courtyard is a barren expanse of cracked stone, surrounded by jagged walls that drip with ash and the occasional spattered blood‑stained rune. Guard barracks flank the entrance, their stone doors bolted shut, the faint clank of iron armor echoing in the cold air.

Beyond the courtyard, a heavy, iron‑bound gate leads into the heart of Azzinoth. The shadow library lies to the left, a dim archive where shelves of forbidden tomes and scrolls are illuminated by the faint glow of phosphorescent lichens, casting trembling shadows that seem to move of their own accord. To the right, the crypt of the Scourge sinks underground; its vaulted chambers are lined with stone coffins and the ossified remains of Radan’s most devoted, the air thick with the scent of incense and decay.

At the very core of the temple lies the Sanctum of Shadows, a circular chamber of obsidian stone where the altar of the Scourge Lord Radan stands upon a plinth of cracked obsidian. Dark, viscous oil pools around the altar, and the walls are etched with ever‑changing sigils that pulse faintly with an unseen power. The whole structure exudes a chill that seeps into bone, a constant reminder that the temple is a place of unending devotion to a lord of plague and ruin.
